coverage.summary: Defaults for annotation validation and risk level tighten in 1.12.0. The environment sets none of the pinning options (clm-638c4e3c1753). The storefront Ingress uses configuration-snippet (clm-669bdaaadac7), a Critical-risk annotation, for PCI security headers. With risk level High it is likely rejected. Pathtype Prefix is fine, and there are no cross-namespace references seen.

The metric removal does not reach this environment. controller.metrics.enabled is false (clm-d7941617bdef). The metric name occurs in no environment file (clm-61ccae29b2aa), so no dashboard, alert or ServiceMonitor references it.

The from-render already passes --enable-metrics=false, so metrics were disabled before the upgrade. The 1.12.0 default is also false, so the chart drops the redundant arg. Effective behaviour is unchanged.

Upstream removes the `plugins` ConfigMap option and /etc/nginx/lua/plugins support. Neither appears in any of the 20 environment artifacts (clm-a08d9d2894ef, clm-a6b4e0444dee). The environment does not use 3rd-party Lua plugins.

The changelog line only says plugins were removed from the Lua lint config (.luacheckrc) and the E2E docs (#11872). That is a development and documentation change. It doesn't change controller runtime behaviour or any rendered setting. No deciding setting exists, and the environment render shows 0 correlated changes. I did not read PR #11872 itself.

The chart removes PSP resources and the podSecurityPolicy.*, existingPsp values. The environment files set none of them (clm-24992bd3bafd, clm-95bd2093fbc6). PSP was also removed from Kubernetes in 1.25, so the cluster (1.31) cannot use it.

The change is an internal refactor: inline Lua is removed from the nginx.tmpl template. The upstream text is a single changelog line and names no setting. The environment's only snippet is the storefront configuration-snippet, which uses more_set_headers (headers-more module) and no Lua. I did not read the Lua code, so I don't know that its behaviour is unchanged. I recorded no claims and requested no validation.

Upstream removes the OpenTelemetry init container/image; the module has been built into the controller image since v1.10 and OTel remains supported. The environment files contain no opentelemetry/otel settings (clm-4f5f15980ebf).

Upstream changelog only says modsecurity coreruleset test files were removed from the nginx image (#11617). Test files are not used at runtime. The environment never mentions modsecurity and does not set enable-modsecurity (clm-a2915f094ad7). No rendered change is correlated to this item.

The changelog line says the Grafana dashboard JSON no longer includes the ingress_upstream_latency_seconds panel/metric. It is a dashboard-only change that affects no runtime workload. No environment file or render references the metric (clm-d1778d2e1fb9). I did not check whether any external alert or dashboard outside the bundle uses it.

agent.budgetRule: item@v1: per item 16 calls, 14 turns, 150000 tokens, 1048576 bytes, 360 s (item defaults 16/14/150000/1MiB/360 s unless AgentConfig.ItemBudget sets them); cap 10 items: 10 of 27 agenda items get a session

agentVerdicts.mechanism: 1.12.0 enables --enable-annotation-validation and lowers annotations-risk-level to High. Critical annotations such as configuration-snippet are then rejected, so the Ingress is not applied to nginx config.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The storefront prod overlay adds a configuration-snippet annotation for PCI security headers. The values files set allowSnippetAnnotations: true but do not set annotations-risk-level, annotation validation, or strict-validate-path-type. The 1.12.0 defaults therefore apply. Both Ingresses use pathType Prefix, so strict path validation is unlikely to matter. catalog-api uses only low-risk annotations.
assumptions: configuration-snippet is classed Critical risk, and allowSnippetAnnotations does not bypass the risk level in 1.12.0. I took both from general knowledge, not from the bundle.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: No runtime evidence. Override inspection was not-run (vr-b94c02bc0f1c).
proposedValidations: runtime: apply the storefront Ingress to a 1.12.0 controller and check admission and config
Set controller.config.annotations-risk-level: Critical, or move the headers to a different mechanism, and re-check
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Upstream source showing allowSnippetAnnotations: true still permits configuration-snippet under the default risk level, or a runtime test showing the Ingress is accepted.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: Controller 1.12.0 stops emitting the already-deprecated Prometheus metric ingress_upstream_latency_seconds. Any dashboard or alert that queries it would go empty.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: Metrics are disabled in the environment values, so the controller exposes no Prometheus endpoint. No environment file references the metric. The removal therefore has no consumer here.
assumptions: No monitoring stack outside the supplied environment files queries this metric.
The Argo CD render does not override metrics.enabled.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: Dashboards or alert rules held outside the bundle could reference the metric. The bundle would not show them.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Metrics enabled for this cluster via another values layer, or an external dashboard or alert rule that uses ingress_upstream_latency_seconds.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: The default of --enable-metrics flips from true to false. This would break environments that rely on metrics being on by default, such as Prometheus scrapes.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The environment's own from-render already ran the controller with --enable-metrics=false. The to-render removes only that redundant arg, so the controller has metrics off both before and after. The override-inspection did not pin because the flag is absent, not because metrics were on.
assumptions: No monitoring depends on the metrics endpoint, which was already off.
The removed arg is not re-added elsewhere in the to-render.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: I did not inspect the to-render for the metrics port or ServiceMonitor objects.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Evidence that metrics were actually enabled before the upgrade, or that the to-render adds a metrics consumer that needs them.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: The `plugins` config option and user Lua plugin directory are removed, so any plugin configured would silently stop working.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: No `plugins` key and no reference to the plugin directory in the environment files. No rendered change is correlated to this item. The environment does not exercise the feature.
assumptions: No custom image or mounted volume injects Lua plugins outside the supplied files.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: Custom controller images or out-of-repo mounts cannot be seen in the bundle.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Evidence of a plugins entry in the controller ConfigMap, or a volume or init container populating /etc/nginx/lua/plugins.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: Lint config and E2E documentation cleanup. It has no runtime effect on the controller.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The change touches only the lint config and the E2E docs, so it should not alter the behaviour of the Ingress objects storefront/storefront and catalog-api/catalog-api. The environment render shows 0 correlated changes. I made no claims about the environment's settings.
assumptions: The changelog title accurately describes #11872, which I did not read.
The change does not remove any Lua plugin mechanism at runtime.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: The text is heuristically classified as a removal. The word 'plugins' could in theory refer to runtime Lua plugins.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: PR #11872 shows that runtime Lua plugin loading was removed, or the environment uses custom Lua plugins.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: Chart no longer ships PSP resources or the podSecurityPolicy.enabled and existingPsp values. Setting them has no effect, or they are rejected by schema validation.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: No environment file sets podSecurityPolicy or existingPsp, so there is no stale value to break or be ignored. Kubernetes 1.31 has no PSP API, so no PSP could have been in use.
assumptions: The 20 environment artifacts searched cover all values the Argo CD source uses.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: Low. Values files not captured in the bundle would not have been searched.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: A podSecurityPolicy or *.existingPsp value set in a values source outside the bundle, or an external RBAC binding that relies on the chart's PSP ClusterRole.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: The inline Lua blocks in the nginx template were removed. This is an internal template change with no user-facing setting.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The environment sets no Lua-based customisation. The one configuration-snippet uses more_set_headers, which is not Lua. The rendered diffs show nothing attributable to this item.
assumptions: The refactor preserves runtime behaviour, as the changelog implies.
The nginx.tmpl template is not overridden by the environment.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: No source diff was available, and the validators did not run.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Evidence that #11806 changed generated nginx.conf behaviour, or a custom template or Lua snippet in the environment.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: The init container and image that installed the OTel module at startup are removed. This breaks only deployments that still depend on that init container or image.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: No OpenTelemetry configuration appears anywhere in the environment files. The module is built into the controller image, so the environment does not use the removed image.
assumptions: No custom extraInitContainers or image references to the removed OTel init image exist outside the searched artifacts.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: Controller-behaviour item, so render silence is not proof.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Any reference to the opentelemetry init image, or an enable-opentelemetry setting that relied on the init container, in the environment.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: Test files removed from the controller image; only something that read those files from the image would break.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The environment files contain no modsecurity configuration (clm-a2915f094ad7), so ModSecurity is not enabled and nothing there would read the removed test files. No rendered change is attributable to this item.
assumptions: No workload or script reads the coreruleset test files from the image.
Changelog wording is the only upstream evidence; PR #11617 was not read.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: Only the changelog line was read. No override-inspection or runtime validation ran.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: Evidence that a workload, init container or custom config references the coreruleset test paths in the controller image, or that ModSecurity is enabled via a ConfigMap or annotation outside the scanned files.

agentVerdicts.mechanism: The shipped Grafana dashboard drops a legacy upstream-latency panel/metric reference. The controller's traffic handling is unchanged.
agentVerdicts.environmentReasoning: The metric name appears in none of the 20 environment artifacts, so no environment alert, rule or dashboard here depends on it. The two Ingress roots are only reconciled by the controller and consume no dashboard.
assumptions: No monitoring rules outside the bundle use this metric.
The removal is only in the dashboard JSON, not in the exported controller metric.
agentVerdicts.uncertainty: The upstream text is a single line. I did not read PR #11878.
agentVerdicts.wouldOverturn: An external alert, recording rule or custom dashboard that queries ingress_upstream_latency_seconds.
